overview: Drishtivada is considered one of the twelve Angas, which are the primary canonical texts in Jainism. It is traditionally attributed to the teachings of Lord Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara. Drishtivada is unique among the Angas as it is said to contain a vast array of knowledge, encompassing subjects beyond spiritual teachings, including cosmology, philosophy, and the natural sciences. Unfortunately, Drishtivada is classified as a lost text, meaning that the original manuscripts, as well as their direct translations, are not available in contemporary times. Jain scholars and adherents rely on references found in other Jain texts and commentaries to understand its content and significance. It is believed that Drishtivada was divided into five sections, with the last section, Purvas, being particularly revered for containing profound philosophical doctrines.

primary_sources.title: Nandisutra
primary_sources.author: Unknown
primary_sources.original_text: दृष्टिवादो य: पुरा प्रवर्तितो जिनैर्महाकल्पानि च
primary_sources.transliteration: dṛṣṭivādo yaḥ purā pravartito jinairmahākalpāni ca
primary_sources.translation: Drishtivada, which was taught by the Jinas, contained great doctrines.
primary_sources.notes: The Nandisutra provides indirect evidence of Drishtivada's existence and its esteemed position in the Jain canon.

misconceptions.myth: Drishtivada is fully available and practiced today.
misconceptions.reality: Drishtivada is a lost text, with no complete manuscripts available. Knowledge of it comes from references in other Jain texts.
